subject: Action needed: Team Nebula Hermes lost its Codex sign-in (neb-ops-gcp)
ticket_title: Codex sign-in lost — Team Nebula Hermes (neb-ops-gcp)
runbook: A HUMAN MUST DO THIS. It cannot be automated and nothing will
self-heal: OpenAI now mandates 2FA on sign-in, so the login has to be completed
by a person at a browser. Until someone runs these steps the bot stays down.
2. Start the device-code login in the default Hermes home:
3. It prints https://auth.openai.com/codex/device plus a short code. Open the URL
in any browser, enter the code, sign in, and complete the 2FA challenge.
Run it under tmux if your session might drop — the process must stay alive to
receive the token, and 2FA makes this step slower than the CLI's default wait.
If it gives up before you finish, re-run with a longer --timeout.
4. Confirm it landed (do NOT trust `auth status`, it reports "logged in" even when
hermes auth list          # want: openai-codex credentials in the active pool
hermes -z "Reply with exactly one word: PONG"
context_note: Why this needs a person: the only repair is a full re-login, which OpenAI now gates
behind 2FA. There is no unattended path back. Do not wait for it to recover by itself.
This box has fallback providers. A broken Codex credential can route work onto a paid
provider, so treat the alert as a reliability and cost issue even if Nebby still answers.
Use a FRESH authorization, not a copy of the one src holds. Both boxes previously
shared one OAuth lineage, and whichever refreshes last silently invalidates the other —
that is what caused the July outage. The credential `label` field is cosmetic and reads
the same on both boxes; compare the refresh-token fingerprint printed in this alert.
quota_subject: Action needed: Team Nebula Hermes is out of Codex quota (neb-ops-gcp)
quota_ticket_title: Codex quota exhausted — Team Nebula Hermes (neb-ops-gcp)
quota_note: This box has fallback providers. Codex quota exhaustion can move work to a paid route,
so confirm the active provider before treating a successful reply as recovery.
@Teamnebula_bot and @Screddy_bot are on SEPARATE ChatGPT accounts. Check which one this
credential is attached to before upgrading anything: on 2026-08-15 the tmn credential was
signed in through "Continue with Google" onto an account with no plan at all, and the
device page reuses whatever ChatGPT session the browser already has — so it re-attached
the same free account twice without ever showing an account picker. Use a private window.
Plus caps are a 7-day rolling window, so a reset can be days out, not hours.
